**The shape of the question.** *«**De Francescijev**» is an Italian surname put into a Croatian possessive — **a name inherited and adapted, not one coined in Croatian**. That points at the name arriving before the Croatian period, i.e. under **Hungarian Fiume** (when it was Zichy) or **Italian Fiume, 1924–45**.*

**⚠ A third candidate, found the same afternoon — and it was already in this archive's own files.**

**[Ferencz Defranceschi](/rijeka/), *révkapitány* — port captain — in the service of the Fiume Maritime Authority, to 1857.** *The Hungarian parliamentary pension schedule of 1872 credits him with **42 years, 10 months and 5 days** of public service and a pension of **1,050 forints** from 1857, which puts him into state service about **1814**; the later accounts style him ***m. kir.* révkapitány**, Royal Hungarian.* **His daughter Francziska was still drawing a 65-forint orphan's *kegydíj* in 1900.**

**Why this is the strongest of the three.** *A pier in Fiume harbour is **port infrastructure**, and the man it honours would most naturally be **a port official of Fiume** — not an Istrian historian and not an unidentified shipowner. **Ferencz is a documented port captain of that exact authority**, serving through the decades before the harbour was rebuilt, and the pier's own Hungarian-era name, **Mol Zichy**, sits in the same administration.*

**⚠ And it is still not evidence.** *No source yet found connects Ferencz to this pier or to any pier. **The case is entirely circumstantial — the right office, the right port, the right era** — and this archive has spent today learning what happens when proximity is mistaken for proof. **(open, and the likeliest of three.)**

**The uncomfortable part.** *Ferencz has been on [/rijeka/](/rijeka/) since 13 September. The pier has been on [/namesakes/](/namesakes/) for as long. **Nobody put them in the same sentence**, because the question lived in a search log and the answer lived in a cluster file — the same failure this session has now met three times in one day.*

**Two further hypotheses, neither adopted.**
· **[Carlo de Franceschi (1809–1893)](/person/carlo-de-franceschi-1809/)**, the Istrian historian and politician — *the most celebrated bearer of the name in the region, and exactly the sort of figure Italian Fiume named civic features after.* **Against it:** he is an **Istrian** public man, not a Fiume port figure, and a working cargo pier is an odd memorial for a historian.
· **A Fiume port or shipping De Franceschi** — *this archive holds **117 people of the name at Rijeka/Fiume**, and [item 143](/worklist/) is already trying to sort two of them out.* **Against it:** none of them is yet shown to be prominent enough.

**What would settle it, in order of cheapness:**
1. **When was it renamed?** *A pier does not change its name silently. **Rijeka port authority chronologies and the city's street-and-quay renaming decrees** would date it, and the date alone would choose between Hungarian, Italian and Yugoslav naming conventions.*
2. **Državni arhiv u Rijeci** — *the city archive, which the September note already said «would settle it».*
3. **Italian-era Fiume directories and the port's own 1924–45 plans**, where an Italian «Molo De Franceschi» would be printed in full.

**⚠ And a caution worth keeping.** *A landmark carrying the surname is **not evidence of this family**. The archive keeps [/namesakes/](/namesakes/) precisely for bearers of the name who are nobody's ancestor, and this pier belongs there until a document ties it to somebody.*

---

**28 September 2026, later — worked, and the leading candidate demoted.**

**The pier now has a construction file:** *it belongs to **Antal Hajnal's** western-shore programme for the Hungarian royal port office — «Istarsko, Bečko, Budimpeštansko i Praško pristanište te **De Francheschijev i Visinov gat**» — **four wharves named for places, two gats named for people**. Warehouse 17 on the Visinov gat is 1906–07, by Ferenc Pfaff. **⚠ The city's page does not say who either man was.***

**⚠ And Ferencz got weaker.** *The **1848** Hungarian directory has the **Fiume harbour captaincy under «Kapitány Sgardelli Alajos»** while **Defranceschi Ferencz headed the Martinšćica quarantine institute**; his «révkapitány» title appears only at his 1857 pensioning, filed under the **Fiume Maritime Authority — the authority for the whole Littoral, not a posting**. **«Port captain of Fiume» is withdrawn as a description**, and Hajnal's programme is decades after he retired.* **Not eliminated; no longer comfortable.**

**Hungaricana nil on five pier terms, controls passing** — *listed in [Searched](/searched/). Weak evidence either way: it is a portal of salaries, not quaysides.*

**Next, in order:** *Državni arhiv u Rijeci; the city's quay-renaming decrees; the Italian-era port plans 1924–45. The Lučka uprava chronology returned **HTTP 520** and should be retried.*

**Lučka uprava retried — nil, and the route is now exhausted.** *520 to a fetcher, fine in a browser. The whole chronology 1717–2025 **names no pier of the Hungarian era**; the first quay named is Orlandov gat, 2013.* **Two dates gained: 1867** *(the basin begun — ten years after Ferencz retired)* **and 1941–45** *(«porušila sve vezove» — every berth destroyed, rebuilt 1950, which is a natural renaming moment and fits the Croatian possessive «De Francescijev»).* **⚠ That sits against the City of Rijeka attributing the name to Hajnal's Hungarian programme; neither is discarded.**

**Remaining, now the shortest list it has ever been:** *Državni arhiv u Rijeci; the city's quay-renaming decrees; the Italian-era port plans 1924–45.*

rows.what: Forty-four findings were made and never told — the search log points at itself
rows.note:
**«Every piece of your work is telling a story about the Defranceschi families and lines, so every new finding needs to be incorporated into that story — otherwise we are here for nothing.»** *David, 28 September 2026. He should not have had to say it, and the number proves it.*

**`scripts/check-story.py` counts it: of **158 searches recorded as hits**, **44 point only at logs** — at [/searched/](/searched/), [/worklist/](/worklist/) or [/corrections/](/corrections/), and never at a person, a line, a household or a topic page.* **Twenty-eight per cent of this archive's findings never reached a reader.**

**They are not trivial ones.** *Among them: the **Wales Roman Catholic marriage** that gave this family a Cosulich; the **Chicago and Memphis households**; **Arolsen's War Time Card File**; the **Crikvenica marriages of 1895 and 1899** and Anna Kalanj's whole household; **Fiume baptisms and burials of 1757 and 1772–74**; the **Svetvinčenat index read end to end**; and **2,251 index rows swept and joined by household**. **Every one of those is a story someone did the work for and nobody told.**

**The distinction the script enforces.** *A **log** is a receipt — what was searched, what was fixed, how. A **story page** is what a reader reads. **A person page counts as story, but a finding that lives only on one person's page has not been told either**, because nobody browses the roster looking for it.*

**What to do, and it is not one job.** *Work the list from the top: for each orphaned hit, either **add an `ev` link to the page where its story is already told**, or — where no such page exists — **write the paragraph**. The second is the real work and the reason this is a worklist item rather than a patch.*

**⚠ The check is wired into the gate as a speaker, not a blocker.** *It prints the count on every build and fails only under `--strict`. **Forty-four pre-existing orphans must not be allowed to block a commit**, or the first thing anyone does is stop running the gate — but the number is now in front of whoever builds, and it should only ever go down.*

---

**28 September 2026, the same day — worked, and the count is zero.**

**Forty-four became zero in one pass, and the shape of the work is worth recording: it was mostly *linking*, not writing.**

| group | n | what it needed |
|---|---|---|
| **Svetvinčenat** | 7 | **links only** — the index reading, Anzoletta, the 1780 households were *already* in the narrative |
| **Fiume / Kastav** | 13 | links **and a paragraph** — the households were on [/rijeka/](/rijeka/), the stories behind them were not |
| **Crikvenica** | 6 | links to [the Crikvenica household](/crikvenica-house/) |
| **Diaspora & Findmypast** | 6 | links to [/diaspora/](/diaspora/) and [/at-sea/](/at-sea/) |
| **DNA, live tree, Arolsen** | 5 | links to [/dna/](/dna/), [/live-tree/](/live-tree/), [/pfullingen/](/pfullingen/) |
| **Households corpus, NSK** | 2 | links to [/households/](/households/) and [/lines/](/lines/) |
| **internal audits** | 3 | **exempted, explicitly** |

**⚠ The one paragraph that had to be written was the Kvarner's.** *Fourteen September searches went to the Fiume film and produced Valentino's household — ten children, five buried — and **none of what made it interesting had been told**: that a **plate** settled the surname where the index wrote it a dozen ways; that four openings were read **at dates no index reaches**, one giving **Ignatio Defranceschi**, a man the index never produced; that **1757** took Maria and raised the question Aloysia's burial answered; and that at one font stood **the wife of the Captain of Kastav**, which is not where a labouring household's godparents come from. **That is now on [/rijeka/](/rijeka/).**

**And the check learned something.** *Three rows were **audits of this archive's own data** — a place string tested against its province, an evidence file checked for orphans — **not findings about the family**. Their honest home is /method/, which is a log by design. They now carry `internal: true` and a stated reason, and the check exempts them **and says how many it exempted**, so the exemption is somebody's decision rather than a silent hole in the count.*

**The number to watch is printed by the gate on every build.** *It is **0**. It should never rise without a reason written down.*

rows.what: The maternal lines have no pages — six women carry «no archive of her own line yet»
rows.note:
**David, 29 September: «what do we know about our core maternal lines? add to your worklist to create them their own family pages».**

**The direct line has six wives, and the front page says the same thing under five of them: *«no archive of her own line yet»*.** *That sentence is the archive admitting a gap in its own shop window.*

| gen | she | born | whose ground |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | **Francisca Salomon** | 17 March 1797 | **this archive** |
| 3 | **Maria née Fernasar** | 17 October 1832 | **this archive** |
| 4 | **Anna Kalanj** | 3 January 1864, **Klenovica in the Vinodol** | **⚠ already has a page — [the Blažević Archive's](https://daviddef.github.io/TheBlazevic/kalanj/)** |
| 5 | **Ursula, born Kovačina** | about 1890 | **this archive** |
| 6 | **Hedviga, born Blažević** | withheld | **[the Blažević Archive's](https://daviddef.github.io/TheBlazevic/)** — the join only |
| 7 | **Cheryl Anne, née Lerena** | living | **another session's** — «Lerena Family Research»; leave it |

**So three pages are this archive's to build: Salomon, Fernasar, Kovačina.** *The other three are already somebody's, and building them here is how an estate ends up with two versions of one woman — [the rule this worklist already set for Hedviga](/worklist/).*

**Done today, because it cost one line:** *the Kalanj door on the front page pointed at the Blažević Archive's **front page**, because the kit derives that door from a surname and the estate's ring only knows whole archives. **It now points at the Kalanj page itself.*** *(`offpage` on generation 4, passed through in `index.astro`; no kit change.)*

**⚠ What this archive actually knows about the three that are its own is thin, and that is the point of the item.**
· **Salomon** — *a birth date, 17 March 1797, and nothing else on the page: no parish, no parents, no siblings.*
· **Fernasar** — *17 October 1832, and the surname is rare enough to be worth a name-study of its own.*
· **Kovačina** — *«about 1890», an estimate, against a husband born at Klenovica house 22; her own parish is not established.*

**And one of them is already entangled with an open question.** *Generation 4 carries a [flag](/): the family's genealogy file gives Josip a wife **Ana Grubišić 1863–1936** with a photographed gravestone, against the **Ana Kalanj** the registers name in all four children's entries. **A Kalanj page cannot be written without settling that**, and the registers govern until a letter says otherwise.*

**Shape of the work, per surname:** *gather every register entry the archive already holds for her; establish her parish; find her parents' marriage; then a page in the shape of the existing family pages, linked from the spine.* **Not started.**

---

**29 September 2026 — David: «I think we should probably have separate pages for each of these women and start researching their families». The pages are built.**

| line | page | what it holds |
|---|---|---|
| **Salomon** | [/maternal/salomon/](/maternal/salomon/) | a birth date, and a family note **now half proved and half withdrawn**: the palace is real and dated 1570; **the parliament seat was never a Salomon's** — it was Carlo De Franceschi's, for Pisino |
| **Fernasar** | [/maternal/fernasar/](/maternal/fernasar/) | **rebuilt 29 Sept to the Kosina shape** — Tornasar retired, the name placed at Gračišće by two casualty lists, and *fornasâr* given a second leg |
| **Kalanj** | [/kalanj/](/kalanj/) | **the fullest of the five** — and building it [corrected a misreading carried in fifteen files](/corrections/) |
| **Kovačina** | [/maternal/kovacina/](/maternal/kovacina/) | **⚠ every document is German paper made after the war**; «about 1890» is an estimate and her birthplace is not established |
| **Blažević** | [/senj-line/](/senj-line/) | the join only; the family is the Blažević Archive's |

**A «Maternal lines» group is now in the navigation.** *⚠ That is **shared ground** — the layout and nav belong to another session — changed on David's explicit request and flagged in the commit.*

**⚠ What these pages are not.** *They are **frames with the evidence that exists**, and each says plainly how thin that is. **No research has been done into any of the three new families yet.** The next step is the same for Salomon and Fernasar — **the Gračišće registers, which are [not on FamilySearch](/corrections/) and need a letter to DAPA or Poreč** — and for Kovačina it is the unread **CM/1 file 32110000 058.158**, «and of further persons».*

rows.what: Anton Defrančeški of Gologorica died at Dachau — is he ours, and is he in Arolsen?
rows.note:
**The Yugoslav victims' census names a man born in this archive's origin parish who died in a German camp, and the archive cannot yet say who he was.**

**What is documented.** *«**Anton Defrančeški**, father **Anton**, born **1909**, born and resident at **Gologorica** in the opština of Pazin, Croat, died **15 July 1944** at **Dachau**, in a camp» — Museum of Genocide Victims, Belgrade, record **2462025028**.* **(doc.)**

**Two questions, and they are cheap.**

**1. Is he in Arolsen?** *⚠ This archive searched [Arolsen on 16 September](/searched/) and found **79 records of the name** while looking for somebody else. **Arolsen holds the Dachau registers.** A man who died in that camp on a stated date should be findable there, and his Arolsen file would carry a prisoner number, a transport, and very often a next of kin — which is exactly what the victims' census does not give.* **This is the single highest-value follow-up on the list.**

**2. Is he ours?** *The [Gologorica–Gračišće line](/gologorica-line/) holds the household the direct line comes out of. **His father was Anton too.** The test is the **Gologorica and Gračišće baptisms around 1909**, which are on film and which this archive can read — the same way the Svetvinčenat marriages were read.* **Until that is done he stays on the line and off the tree.**

**⚠ And a caution.** *A surname in a victims' index is not a relative. This archive keeps [/namesakes/](/namesakes/) for exactly that reason, and the honest outcome here may be that he belongs there.*

---

**29 September 2026 — question 1 answered, and the answer is no.**

**He is not in Arolsen**, under `Defranceschi` (38 people), `Defranceski` (79) or `Defrancesco` (8). *None is born in 1909 at an Istrian place.*

**⚠ Getting there meant disproving a match that looked perfect** — *«DEFRANCESCHI, ANTONIO, 31 January 1909, prisoner 8165», which turned out to be an **ITS cross-reference card** to a file under **DEFRANCESCO**: born at **Moncalvo in Piedmont**, died at Dachau **7 February 1945**, not 15 July 1944.* **[The disproof is on his page](/person/anton-defranceski-of-gologorica-1909-1944-1909/) and [the rule it earned is in the method](/method/).**

**Question 2 is untouched and this item stays open for it.** *Whether he descends from the Gologorica household needs the **Gračišće and Gologorica baptisms of about 1909**, which are on film and readable the same way the Svetvinčenat marriages were.* **That is now the whole of the item.**

**⚠ And the search found a Vodnjan household for somebody else's item:** *the IRO CM/1 Italy files hold **Giuseppe b. 1904 at Dignano**, **Giovanna née Bortolussi b. 1911 at Dignano**, and three children — the town [the two men found yesterday](/lines/) came from.*

---

**⚠ 29 September, later — question 2 cannot be done from a desk, and this item's own instruction was wrong.**

**The correction first.** *This item said the baptisms were «on film». **They are not** — [`waypoints.json`](/searched/) records Gologorica, Gračišće and Pićan as **absent** from FamilySearch's Croatian collection, walked in September. **The route was named without opening a file this archive already held.** [On /corrections/.](/corrections/)*

**The book, named exactly:** **DAPA no. 1166 — Gologorica, MKR, 1880–1948, held at BA Poreč, digitised.** *One volume covers 1909.*

**The errand, ready to send.** *Biskupijski arhiv (Poreč-Pula diocese), **Dobrilina 3, 52440 Poreč** — **ppbarhiv@gmail.com**, archivist **Branka Poropat**, +385 52 635 418.*

> **Ask for:** the **baptism entry of Anton Defrančeški / Defranceschi, born 1909 at Gologorica, father Anton**, from **MKR Gologorica 1880–1948 (DAPA inv. 1166)** — with the **mother's name and maiden surname**, the **house number**, and the **godparents**. *That is what decides whether he belongs to the Gologorica household this archive holds.*

*DAPA's own page says it declines open-ended genealogical research but accepts requests carrying **name, approximate period and place** — this has all three — and this family has [used DAPA successfully twice](/sources/), in April and June 2021, at 117 and 124 kuna including overseas postage.*

**⚠ Blocked, and named:** *Hrčak serves a **«Confirm you're not a robot»** check, so the Trogrlić parish chronicle 1892–1918 — which covers these exact years — was **not** fetched. **This archive does not work around bot checks.** One click for a person.*

**⚠ 29 September 2026 — David: «not sending letters yet.» This item waits on that decision and is not to be raised again until he lifts it.** *Recorded once, here, so no session re-opens it by suggesting the letter afresh.*

---

**30 September 2026 — a possible SECOND ROUTE to question 2, which needs no letter.** *The letter above stays where David left it and is not re-raised.*

This item's only route to the 1909 baptism is the Poreč diocesan archive, because Gologorica is absent from FamilySearch. **But the other collection had never been asked.** The Croatian State Archives' microfilm collection **HR-HDA-1448** — the one [the Brinje work](/searched/) used — **lists GOLOGORICA as a parish**, and GRAČIŠĆE under **four** name forms.

**What it holds for them is unknown**: the search would not run, and this archive does not claim a nil from a tool whose failures look exactly like absences. **[Recorded as a lead to retry](/searched/), not as a finding.** *If Gologorica's films reach 1909, question 2 can be answered from a desk.*

rows.what: Brinje — answered: Anna's baptism is post-1860 and by law never went to an archive
rows.note:
**The baptism of [Anna Kalanj](/kalanj/) says where her people came from, and this archive had never read the phrase.**

> *«Josephus Kalanj et Rosalia nata Perković ejus uxor, **Brinjensis Parochiæ ruricolæ**»* — **country people of the parish of Brinje**, at Kljenovica house 22, entry 2 of 1864, Ledenice. *(doc.)*

**Brinje is inland**, up behind the coast — *so the Kalanj were not Vinodol people; they had come down to Klenovica from the hills, exactly as [this archive's own line came down from Gračišće](/crikvenica-house/) a generation later.*

**⚠ THAT WAS TRUE WHEN THIS ROW WAS WRITTEN AND IS NOT TRUE NOW — see the addition of 29 September below.** The line that follows is kept as it stood.

**⚠ And both family archives are stopped at the same door.** *[The Blažević Archive](https://daviddef.github.io/TheBlazevic/kalanj/) — which holds 215 Kalanj — calls Brinje «**the single largest hole in this family**» and records that «**not one page of its register has been opened**».* **Neither archive has opened it.**

**What it would answer:** *Rosalia née Perković's people, who are [in no archive at all](/tree/); whether [Luka Kalanj 1859–1944](/kalanj/) is Anna's brother; and how far back the Kalanj go before the move to the shore.*

**First step:** *establish whether the Brinje registers are filmed — the archive's own [waypoints walk](/searched/) of the Croatian collection is the place to look — and if not, which archive holds them.* **Not started.**

**⚠ 29 September 2026 — David: «not sending letters yet.» This item waits on that decision and is not to be raised again until he lifts it.** *Recorded once, here, so no session re-opens it by suggesting the letter afresh.*

---

**✅ THE FIRST STEP IS DONE, 29 September 2026: Brinje is filmed, and the film starts too late.**

**HR-HDA-1448**, the Croatian State Archives' supplementary microfilm collection — the same one [the Crikvenica page](/crikvenica-house/) already names — holds Brinje as **five entries and no more**: births **1888–1892**, **1893–1897**, **1897–1900**; marriages **1888–1899**; deaths **1888–1899**. Reels **ZM-34C/681** and **ZM-34C/682**, topographic marks **M-1278** and **M-1279**. **All transcripts. None digitised.**

**Anna was born in 1864.** The films cannot reach her, her parents' marriage, or her siblings. *So the cheap route is closed and the question is now a different one: where are the pre-1888 Brinje books?* **Three candidates, none asked:** the parish office at Brinje, the **diocesan archive of Senj-Modruš**, and the **Državni arhiv u Gospiću**, which covers Lika-Senj county and whose own registers are said to begin in the second half of the eighteenth century.

**⚠ Nine neighbouring parishes were queried and all nine results were thrown away.** Jezerane, Letinac, Stajnica, Prozor, Krivi Put, Vodoteč, Ogulin, Modruš and Crikvenica all returned «Nema zapisa» — *and so did **BRINJE**, which holds five rows, when re-run the same way.* **Setting that search box from script does not commit the value to the server, and the empty result is identical to a real nil.** The control caught it. **Those nine parishes are untested, not empty**, and [the trap is written up in the search log](/searched/) so the next session does not repeat it.

---

**⚠ 29 September 2026 — CORRECTED THE SAME DAY IT WAS WRITTEN. The door was opened a fortnight ago, by the other archive, and this row did not know.**

David: *«Have you looked at the Blažević's session? It's been documenting the Brinje volumes and researching Kalanj in Brinje for a while now.»* **It has.**

· **15 September** — that session located both films: **DGS 5498262** (*Rođeni 1888–1900, Vjenčani 1888–1899*, items 1–4 of roll 2121763) and **DGS 5498263** (*Umrli 1888–1899*). Both begin at item 1, so both are reachable by film number.
· **20 September** — measured that **Brinje has nothing indexed at all**, for any event, under Kalanj or Marić. The village is reachable only by opening the film.
· **29 September** — **images 493 to 622 of 693 read**, waypoint **9R26-82S**. Found: **Kalanj Niko**, of Brinje **house 231**, son of Juro; **Kalanj Mijo**, of **house 249**, born about 1838; **Kalanj Mate** as witness; **Perković Đuso**, daughter of Perković Jozo; and seven **Borić** men across four Brinje hamlets. *None yet tied to Anna's household.*

**So this row's «first step» had been taken, and taking it again produced the same answer.** That is the fourth repeat of this shape today, and the first across archives rather than within one. *The working rules say to grep this archive's logs before claiming a find; they do not say to check the sibling archives, and on this evidence they should.*

**What is genuinely this archive's to do, and nobody is doing it.** Every filmed Brinje book — on either road — begins in **1888**. **Anna was born 3 January 1864** and her parents married before that. Her baptism, their marriage and her brothers and sisters are in **pre-1888 originals that are on no film**. The HDA copies are marked **PRIJEPIS, transcripts**, which says the originals are still with an institution: **the parish office at Brinje**, the **Senj-Modruš diocesan archive**, or the **Državni arhiv u Gospiću**. **None has been asked.** That is the row now.

---

**⚠ 30 September 2026 — THE DATE WALL IS EXPLAINED, and it is a frontier.**

*First, what is not this archive's: **the Blažević session is reading the Brinje registers right now**, image by image — through the marriage book and into the Rođeni volumes, with Kalanj households emerging at houses 231, 249 and 118/189. **That ground is theirs and is not touched here.** `whoelse.sh` confirms no sibling archive has raised the Military Frontier, the 1882 boundary or DAGS-109 for Brinje.*

**Every Brinje series begins at the same moment:** HR-HDA-1448 at **1888** (and all of it *prijepis*, transcripts); Gospić's **HR-DAGS-109** at **1882**, though that collection as a whole runs from **1793**.

**Brinje was in the MILITARY FRONTIER.** *The Ministry of War's authority ended 1 August 1881; administration passed to the Croatian provincial government on **1 January 1882**.* **The registers begin where Brinje stopped being a regiment and became a county** — which is why two unrelated holdings land on the same year.

**Anna was born 1864, so her baptism is in Military Frontier–era books, eighteen years out of reach of both archives.** *Three candidates remain and **none has been asked**: the **parish office at Brinje**, the **diocesan archive of Gospić-Senj** (formerly Senj-Modruš), or they did not survive.* **That is what this item now is.**

**⚠ And two catalogues are gone.** *`arhinet.arhiv.hr` (ARHiNET, also called **NAIS**) does not resolve — **NXDOMAIN**, confirming Record Atlas. `hais.arhiv.hr` **does resolve**, to 161.53.80.20, but serves **nothing on either port 80 or 443**. ⚠ **This item first called HAIS ARHiNET's «successor»; that came from the atlas's note and not from anything checked here, and is withdrawn** — the network state is established, the succession is not. And **www.arhiv.hr is a different machine, 161.53.80.7, and is not the fonds register**: it is the archive's own site plus the one live database. Search engines still index ARHiNET pages; the links are dead. **Hrčak returned HTTP 418** to the study of the HDA's register collection, which is its bot rejection and was not worked around.*

---

**✅ 30 September 2026 — THE QUESTION IS ANSWERED, and the answer is a law.**

*David cleared Hrčak's bot check so the inventory of **HR-HDA-883** could be read — Angelika Milić, Arhivski vjesnik 60 (2017), 251–311.*

> **«Odlukom Ministarstva unutrašnjih poslova NRH od 13. svibnja 1949. određeno je da se sve matične knjige s upisom do 1860. predaju na čuvanje nadležnim arhivima»** — *and the 1946 law gave registers **from 1860** to the matični uredi, «koje su bile potrebne u radu državnim matičnim uredima».*

**Up to 1860 → the archives. From 1860 → left with the registry office.** **Anna was born 3 January 1864.** *Her baptism was never going to be in a state archive's collection. It is not lost; it was left where it was being used.*

**Confirmed on Brinje's doorstep**: the collection holds the **Senj-Modruš** diocese, and its Lika parishes stop exactly at the line — Gospić 1789→**1858/1859**, Senj 1678→**1858**. *And **Brinje does not appear in it at all**.*

**So the item changes shape.** *Not «open Brinje» but: **the matični ured / parish at Brinje** for 1864, and the **Gospić-Senj diocesan archive** for the pre-1860 books that reached no state archive. **No letter is drafted or sent** — David's instruction stands.*

*The inventory also yielded 2,503 volumes across 357 parishes, 1585–1947, catalogued for Record Atlas as provider `hda-883`; the extract was deliberately not committed there because its licence gate refused a dataset whose publisher states no licence.*

rows.what: The maternal lines in books: what can actually be read, family by family
rows.note:
**David, 29 September 2026: «what research can we do in books and deep research for those families?» Worked through, family by family, with what was tested today.**

**SALOMON — the most tractable of the four, and half of it moved today.**
· ✅ **The palace is real**: the **Salamon palace at Gračišće**, sixteenth century, **dated 1570**, Gothic bifore on the first floor. *(doc for the building; the source gives no family history.)*
· ✅ **SETTLED THE SAME DAY, and the answer was no.** *David downloaded the roll of the 422 deputies himself — the mechanical block was on this session, not on the document.* **There is no Salomon in it**, and the negative is properly made: *437 lines, **65 surnames beginning with S**, zero matches for Salomon or Salamon in any spelling, with the control passing.* **And a Defranceschi IS in it:** «*Defranceschi · Karl · k.k. Rathsprotokollist · **Pisino** · Küstenland*» — **[Carlo De Franceschi](/carlo/), and the roll gives the constituency his page never had.** *The family remembered a seat in the Vienna parliament correctly for a century and a half and attached it to the wife's people. [The correction is on /corrections/](/corrections/).*
· **[Bertoša, «Gologorički De Franceschi», 1985](/sources/)** — *76 pages, «the most important single thing still unread» by this archive's own reckoning. **Not online.** A Croatian library or ILL.*
· **The palace as a listed monument**: *Croatian conservation literature — **the Seget precedent**, where Puhmajer's monograph came free from the Ministry of Culture, is the model.*

**FERNASAR — a book could settle this WITHOUT a register.**
· ✅ **DONE 29 September 2026, and the prediction in it was wrong.** *Both national surname databases were asked — the Croatian 2011 census and Cognomix's 180,000 Italian surnames — and **neither Fernasar nor Tornasar exists in either**, so no atlas of the present can choose between them; the palaeography was **not** decided from the armchair.* **What it did do is remove Tornasar's last support**: printed in no issue of anything, borne by nobody. *And it put a second leg under the* ***fornasâr*** *etymology — **Fornasar is real: 25 Italian families, 8 of them in Friuli-Venezia Giulia and 4 in the Veneto.*** **[The terms tried, with controls, are in the search log](/searched/); the page is [/maternal/fernasar/](/maternal/fernasar/).** *What is still open is the ink: her own baptism of 17 October 1832 as an image.*

**KOVAČINA — the document is already identified and unread.**
· **Arolsen CM/1 `3.2.1.1, ref 32110000 058.158`** — *«Personal file of DEFRANCESKI, PETAR… **and of further persons**». **«Further persons» is where a wife's birthplace gets written down**, and this file has never been opened.* **Free, online, no letter required.**

**KALANJ / PERKOVIĆ — both archives stopped at one door.**
· **[Brinje](/worklist/)** — *item 161. Neither this archive nor Blažević has opened a page of it.*
· *Rosalia née Perković is [in no archive at all](/tree/).*

**⚠ What «deep research» would and would not help with.** *Three of these four are **not** questions the open web can answer — they need a register, a subscription archive, or a physical book. **The exceptions are exactly two**: the Reichstag list (a PDF that wants opening) and the Fernasar/Tornasar surname question (a reference-book question). **Those two are worth a research pass; the rest want letters and a library.*** **Not started.**

rows.what: One markdown renderer, not twenty-five — and 152 tables that print as pipes
rows.note:
**Found while building the Kalanj page: this archive writes markdown tables into its data and most of its pages cannot render them.** **⚠ The symptom.** *`|---|` printed literally on **/lines/**, **/corrections/**, **/method/**, **/worklist/**, **/people/** and twenty-odd person pages. **152 table blocks** are written into the data — 97 in `searched.json` alone, across many sessions — and they have never displayed as tables.* **Half-fixed on 29 September.** *Table support was added to the shared **`site/src/lib/md.js`**, and **/searched/ now renders 59 tables** where it printed pipes. ⚠ *That file is **shared ground** by `whose.sh`'s reckoning — it falls through to the catch-all — and the change was made and flagged.* **⚠ The root cause is bigger, and it is the real item.** *There is **not one renderer**. There are **twenty-five**: `1948`, `at-sea`, `carlo`, `changes`, `cheryl-lerena`, `corsica`, `corrections`, `dna`, `errands`, `gaps`, `fiume-1626`, `liznjan`, `method`, `imperial`, `julius`, `photograph-these`, `register`, `rijeka`, `marriages`, `tree`, `trentino`, `vodnjan`, `the-eleven` and the `Cluster` and `Household` components **each define their own `const md = (s) => …`**, while **42 pages import the shared one**.* **So a fix to the renderer reaches 42 pages and misses 25.** *Every local copy has drifted separately; this is why [links printed as literal brackets for a year](/method/) and why tables print as pipes now. **The same bug has to be fixed twenty-six times or once.*** **The work:** *replace each local `md` with an import of `site/src/lib/md.js`, page by page, checking each page's output before and after.* ⚠ **Not a five-minute job and not one to do at the end of a long session** — *several of those pages pass extra transforms (`based`, `link`) around their local renderer, and those have to be preserved.* **Not started.** --- **29 September 2026 — fourteen of twenty-five done, and the other eleven are blocked on the data, not the code.** **⚠ The refactor turned out to have a fork in it that the item had not seen.** *The local renderers **do not escape**; the shared one does. And **twenty data files contain intentional raw HTML** — ``, ``, `` — which renders today **because** those pages do not escape. **Swapping them blind would have turned that markup into visible tag text.*** **So the pages were split by their data, and only the safe half converted:** | | | |---|---| | **converted** | trentino · at-sea · the-eleven · vodnjan · marriages · fiume-1626 · imperial · carlo · cheryl-lerena · errands · julius · photograph-these · rijeka · Cluster | | **blocked on data** | changes · 1948 · gaps · register · corrections · corsica · liznjan · tree · dna · method | **Verified by diffing the built HTML of every converted page before and after.** *All thirteen diffs are **improvements or cosmetic**: `errands` changed single to double quotes on a style attribute; **`rijeka` had been printing literal asterisks and now renders italics**; the rest are byte-identical or near. **No escaped-tag leakage on any of them.*** **`mdps()` was added to the shared lib** — *a paragraph break carrying a style — because four pages kept a private copy of the whole renderer purely to get `

`.* **⚠ What is left is a DATA job, not a code job.** *The eleven remaining pages cannot move until the raw HTML in their data is migrated to markdown — a raw anchor tag becoming a markdown link, and the `` markers becoming something the renderer knows. **That is the real remainder of this item**, and it also fixes a latent bug found on the way: `method.json` contains **`

rows.what: Eight pages scrolled sideways on a phone; none do now
rows.note:
**David asked for a run through the main pages on mobile and web. All 98 were swept at 375px and 1440px, in iframes, measuring `scrollWidth` against the viewport.**

**✅ Desktop is clean: 0 of 98 overflow at 1440px.**

**Mobile started at 15 of 98 and is now 8.** *Fixed: `/errands/` (359px over), `/live-tree/` (204), `/sources/` (160 → 8), `/findmypast/`, `/corrections/`, `/changes/`, `/old-site/`, `/method/`.*

**What the fixes were, and one thing worth knowing.** *Wide tables were never in a `.scroll` container — including **the tables this archive started rendering the same day**, which is how a content fix became a layout bug. And the long unbreakable tokens carried `white-space:nowrap`, against which `overflow-wrap` is powerless.* **⚠ The nowrap rules are Astro SCOPED styles from kit components** — *`.er-tag[data-astro-cid-…]`, a class-plus-attribute selector that outranks anything this stylesheet can write, in a kit that belongs to another session.* **So `!important` is used, deliberately, in that one media query, and the reason is written above it.**

**⚠ And one of the fixes made things worse before it made them better.** *`table thead, table tbody { width: max-content }` is a standard responsive-table trick and it **added** overflow here — `/corsica/` went to 310px over. Reverted. So did forcing `.num` to wrap: `/method/` went from 25px over to 129px, because a reference number that breaks mid-digit is not an improvement. **Both are recorded rather than quietly dropped.***

**The eight that remain, with what is known about each:**

| page | over | what is wide |
|---|---|---|
| `/corsica/` | **310** | a `TBODY` — the hand-written table is not in a `.scroll` |
| `/cheryl-lerena/` | **252** | **nothing over 8px wide was found** — the cause is not an element box |
| `/worklist/` | **163** | same: no wide element found |
| `/households/` | **50** | same |
| `/` | **33** | the sovereignty `svg`, min-width 940px |
| `/crikvenica-house/` | 9 | a `TBODY` |
| `/sources/` | 8 | a `TBODY` |
| `/who/giovanni-defranceschi/` | 3 | a `THEAD` |

**⚠ The interesting ones are the three where no wide element could be found.** *`scrollWidth` exceeds the viewport but every box measures inside it — which points at a margin, a negative offset or a transform rather than a wide child. **The `.bleed` and `.scroll` breakout rules use `margin-left:50%; transform:translateX(-50%)`**, and that is the first thing to test.* **Not started.**

---

**✅ CLOSED 29 September 2026 — 0 over, at three widths.**

**And the number above was wrong when it was written, which is the more useful half of this.** The preview server serves a *staged copy* of `dist`, and it had not been re-staged after the rebuild, so «15 down to 8» was measured partly against older output. Every figure below is from a build staged immediately before the sweep.

| swept | 375px | 768px | 1280px |
|---|---|---|---|
| **210** top-level, second-level, all 50 place pages | **0** | **0** | **0** |
| **496** `/person/` and `/who/` pages | **0** | — | — |

**Four faults, each found by hiding elements one at a time until the page stopped overflowing, then measuring min-content of what was left.**

· **The home page, 33px.** A cross-archive door label *I* had written that morning — 49 characters in a kit component whose `.dsc-door` is `nowrap`. Every other label on the page is 21–34. **The kit was not at fault and was not touched**; the label was shortened.
· **Five `/people/` biographies, up to 505px.** The `.rec` grid's third cell is built for a short mono note; these pages put sentences in it. *«Lamberta carries his own mother's name.»* is 642px of nowrap.
· **Six `/who/` pages, 14–35px — caused by my own first attempt at the line above.** **Two unrelated components share the class name `.rec`**, and an unscoped rule collapsed the other one's second track to 0px. Scoped to `.rec-bio`.
· **`/places/vizinada/`, 5px.** The mobile rule used a bare `1fr`, **whose implicit minimum is min-content**, so the single column sized itself to 362px inside a 324px box. Now `minmax(0,1fr)`.

**Still over at 320px: the home page, by 8px.** Below the 375px target and recorded rather than claimed as clean.

rows.what: Two Maria Defranceschi of Gologorica share a birthday nine years apart — walk July 1780 and July 1789

*The test named here was: walk July 1780 and July 1789 in the baptism books, both of which are on the reel. **July 1789 has her.***

> **«Maria Rosa=/lia Defrances=/chi ex Loco»**, house **36**, father **«Joh: Baptis[ta]»**, mother **«Catharina Joblich»**, godmother **«Rosalia Baxa uxor Petri ex Lindar»** *(ZM34K-214, M01069020)*.
