rows.what: BAKAR — read it properly, now that a wife of the direct name is documented as coming out of it
rows.note:
**David, 30 September 2026: «add bakar to our next to read worklist».** *Raised the same hour a Bakar woman was documented marrying a Defranceschi of Gologorica.*

**⭐ THE NEW REASON.** *The Gologorica baptism register, 3 October 1786, enters as godparents* **«Joh: Bapt. Defranceschi m.p. · Cath. ejus uxor nata **JABLICH ex BUCCARI**»**, *both* **Cives Gollogoricenses**. **Catharina, wife of Joannes Baptista Defranceschi, was born a Jablich of Bakar** — a hundred and thirty kilometres and a different sovereignty from the Istrian interior. *[She is on the roster](/married-in/); **Jablich appears nowhere else in this archive**.* *(doc — DAPA ZM34K-214, M01069017.)*

**⚠ Bakar is not a new front. It is a front this archive has left half-open, and the pieces have never been put beside each other:**

| what | where it stands |
|---|---|
| **Bakar parish registers** | *pending, **never opened**, and the family's own recollection points at them* |
| **FamilySearch, Bakar country** | ***eight entries***, found only when the sweep was re-run with deep paging — the first run returned one |
| **An 1849 Bakar baptism** | *reads* **«Francisci Defranceschi **Regii**»** — *the word that started the royal-office inference, since corroborated on Hungaricana* |
| **«Stemmi della nobiltà di Buccari»**, *Bakarski zbornik* 2 (1996) | *pending — **fifty-seven pages on the arms of Bakar's patrician houses**, and this archive has an [arms page](/arms/) resting on a lintel and a stone* |
| **ANNO, «Defranceschi» + «Buccari»** | ***blocked*** — nine issues named and dated, reader behind a bot check. **Not to be worked around.** |
| **«Galeb» and «Kvarner»**, the two Bakar newspapers | ***a genuine nil***, controls passed. Settled; do not re-run. |
| **British shipping press, «Buccari»** | **1,377 articles, all shipping** — Bakar had its own standing heading in London from at least the 1860s |

**What to do, in order:**

1. **Establish whether the Bakar registers are filmed at all**, and by whom — *the [HDA supplementary microfilm search](/searched/) answers that question for any Croatian parish, and it has never been asked about Bakar.* **Drive the place box through real UI interaction and run a known-positive control first**; *script-setting that combo box manufactured nine false nils on 29 September.*
2. **Look for Jablich, not only for the surname.** *A marriage of a Jablich daughter to a Joannes Baptista Defranceschi, before 1786, is a specific entry in a specific decade — far more findable than a surname sweep.*
3. **The** *Bakarski zbornik* **article**, *which is a library request rather than an archive one.*

**Not started.** *No letter is to be sent on this until David lifts the hold.*

rows.what: VOLOSCA — five films already catalogued here with waypoints, and not one of them ever opened
rows.note:
**David, 30 September 2026: «Have we ever gone through the volosca books?»** *The answer is no, and the sharper answer is that **this archive already holds the waypoints and has never used them**.*

`kvarner-books.json` *carries* **Volosko (Opatija)** *with five films, its* `books` *array empty and its* `why` *blank — nothing read, no reason recorded. Across 474 searches Volosca appears in two, and one of those was written this morning.*

| book | waypoint |
|---|---|
| Births 1791–1831 | `9R28-3YD` |
| Births 1831–1886 | `9R28-3Y7` |
| Deaths 1792–1831, baptisms 1841/1845/1846 | `9R28-PY8` |
| Deaths 1831–1902, 1927 | `9R28-PY7` |
| **Marriages 1792–1906** | **`9R28-3T1`** |

**⭐ WHY IT MATTERS NOW.** *The 1826* status animarum *enters* **«Lambertina uxor nata Peschle»** *with* **«Ex Volosca»** *against her — [Carlo De Franceschi's mother](/gologorica-line/), and the town every printed life of him names.*

**⚠ But the obvious target is not there, and saying so first saves a wasted sitting.** *Her birth was established on 30 September as* **17 September 1786** *from the household book. **The Volosko births film begins in 1791.** Her own baptism is five years before the film starts.*

**What IS in range, in order of sharpness:**

1. **The marriage of 3 February 1807** — *Josephus Defranceschi and Lambertina Peschle. Weddings are normally in the bride's parish, and* **Marriages 1792–1906 (`9R28-3T1`) covers it**. *It would name her father.* **This is the one to open first.**
2. **Alexander Peschle, b. 1803**, *son of Mathias Peschle and Justina Jacich — the oldest Peschle this archive holds, and* **Births 1791–1831 covers him**.
3. **Deaths 1792–1831** *for Mathias and Justina's generation.*

*Held until the 1826* status animarum *is finished, per the rule adopted the same day: **finish the book you opened before opening another**.*

rows.what: KRBUNE — «Cherbune» in the register, and where the Grah/Grach came from
rows.note:
**David, 1 October 2026: «So Cherbune for the grah family? Would it be worth adding to your worklist the records to search from here».** *Yes — and the place is identifiable.*

**⭐ Where it came from.** *The Gologorica baptism of* **Franciscus Antonius Defranceschi, 13 April 1785, house 31** *— son of Joannes Baptista and* **Theresia née Grach** *— has as godfather* **«Archipresbiter GRACH» of «Cherbune»**. *The mother's own kin, and a churchman: **an archpriest in the Grach family was not known here**.* *(doc — ZM34K-214, M01069015.)*

**⚠ «Cherbune» is NOT Cerovlje.** *The same register writes Cerovlje separately and differently —* «Cerougl», «Cerouglie», «Ceroughe», *and the 1826 census has* «In comunitate **Corougliensi**». **«Cherbune» is KRBUNE**, *a village at* **45.2569 N, 14.0472 E** — *about four kilometres from Gologorica, in the same tight cluster as Gračišće and Cerovlje.*

**What there is to read, and it is thin.** *The [Record Atlas](../Record Atlas) holds* **one** *collection for Krbune against 22 for Gologorica, 24 for Cerovlje and 32 for Gračišće:*

> **Births 1803–1869 · Deaths 1803–1870 · Marriages 1803–1870**, Roman Catholic, one bound volume.
> **FamilySearch waypoint `9R2Z-92G`.** *Never opened by this archive.*

**⚠ And the obvious target is out of range, which is worth saying before anyone sits down to it.** *The archpriest stands at the font in* **1785**; *the film begins in* **1803**. **He is eighteen years before it.** *What the volume WOULD carry is the generation after him — and a* **Marianna Grah, daughter of Mathias and Justina, born 19 September 1834**, *is already recorded in the Gologorica census, so the family was still in the district.*

**Why the Grah matter to this family:** *Theresia née Grach is the mother of the* **casa 31** *household — one of the two Joannes Baptista houses, now told apart by their wives — and a* **Catharina Defranceschi nata Grach** *stands godmother in the 1787 baptisms. [The Grach have no married-in page](/married-in/).*

**Order of work:** *1. the Krbune volume `9R2Z-92G` for Grah/Grach entries after 1803; 2. Gračišće and Cerovlje, which are better covered and next door; 3. an archpriest is a diocesan record — the **Poreč-Pula** clergy lists would name him and give his dates.*

---

**⭐ 5 October 2026 — KRBUNE WAS A PARISH IN ITS OWN RIGHT, and its priest came to Gologorica.**

*Folio 119 of the Gologorica baptism book, 1 February 1858 (DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01069133): the* baptizans *column, which has read* «Petrus Milcetich, Parochus» *for twenty-three years, names for one entry* **«Franciscus P— Ad.r PAR. CHERBUNIS»** — ***the administrator of the parish of Krbune***.

**Why it matters to this item.** *The worry behind worklist 168 was that Krbune's single bound volume might be a fragment, or the place a chapelry of somewhere else — one collection against thirty-two for Gračišće is the kind of imbalance that usually means the records went elsewhere.* ***This shows Krbune with its own administrator, standing in for a neighbouring parish.*** **A parish that lends a priest keeps a register**, *and the volume the atlas lists — births, deaths and marriages* **1803–1870** — *is the right book for the place and not somebody else's leavings.*

**⚠ The priest's surname is NOT published.** *It reads as* **Pasnich**, **Papich** *or* **Bascich**, *and has not been set against the same hand writing any of those elsewhere. [A hand is only legible against itself](/method/); the office and the parish are plain and carry the point without it.* **If it is settled later it is worth having** — *a named Krbune administrator of 1858 is a person to ask the Pazin archive about.*

**⭐ 5 October 2026, same walk — a second word attached to the Grah.**

*Folio 123 of the Gologorica baptism book, 20 May 1862 (DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01069137): the mother is entered* **«Mariana Grah»** *with* **«Missan»** *written beneath the surname, and a godmother* **«Cathar. Grah»** *with* **«missan»** *beneath hers.*

**⚠ Whether «Missan» is a byname or a place is NOT settled here**, *and it is claimed as neither.* *This register uses both constructions —* «Flegar **alias** Jacotich» *and* «Flegar **alias** Sidre» *for bynames,* «ex Cerouglie» *and* «Ex Parochia Gallignanæ» *for places — and this entry uses neither word, only position.*

**WHY IT IS RECORDED ANYWAY.** *The Grah are the family behind this item, and* ***a second word attached to a common surname is exactly what makes one findable in a register***. *If* **Missan** *is a byname it should recur beside Grah in the Krbune volume; if it is a place it should be identifiable near Krbune.* **Either answer is useful and the test is the same: look for the pair, not the surname.**

**⭐ 5 October 2026, later — FIVE attestations of a Krbune priest, and one of them is NAMED.** *Reading the strip at the foot of each page, which [this archive had been cropping off](/corrections/), turned up the parish of Cherbune over and over in the* baptizans *column:*

| when | frame | who |
|---|---|---|
| **29 Nov 1832** | M01069106 | **«Franciscus Xaverius, Parochus CHERBUNENSIS»** |
| **19 Feb 1841** | M01069115 | *«ex permissione … Parochus Cherbunensis»* |
| **11 Jul 1842** | M01069116 | *«Parochus Cherbunensis»* |
| **2 Oct 1848** | M01069123 | **«Josephus Dekalice(?), Administrator parochialis CHERBUNES»** |
| **1 Feb 1858** | M01069133 | *«Franciscus P—, Ad.r Par. Cherbunis»* |

***Krbune had a parish priest of its own for at least twenty-six years***, *and he was close enough to Gologorica to baptise there five times over.* **Whatever worry remained that its single bound volume might be a fragment is gone.**

**⚠ Two surnames are offered and neither is settled**: *the 1832* **Franciscus Xaverius** *is a given name with no surname written, and the 1848* **Dekalice** *has had no second construction. [A hand is only legible against itself](/method/).* **The offices, the parish and the dates are plain and carry the point.**

rows.what: The DEANERY VISITATION records — a whole record series this archive did not know existed
rows.note:
**Found on 1 October 2026 while closing gaps in the Gologorica baptism book.** *Twice the register is interrupted by a certificate ruled across the page and signed by the rural dean:*

> **«Revisus in Visitatione decanali die 17ma Julii 1804»** — *M. **Franciscus Franovich**, Canonicus, Regius Parochus et **Decanus***
> **«Revisus et approbatus in Visitatione Decanali 25 Junii 1808»** — ***Petrus Anicich**, Canonicus, Parochus et **Decanus***

**The parish books were inspected and signed off by a dean.** *An inspection that signs a book generates a record of its own: **visitation protocols** name the parish, its priest, its fabric, its souls and often its failings. **This archive holds none and did not know to look.***

**Where they would be.** *Gologorica was in the diocese of **Pićan (Pedena)** until its suppression in 1788, then **Poreč-Pula**. Visitation records of both are the kind of thing held by the **diocesan archive at Poreč** — [already on the errands list for other reasons](/errands/) — and by the **Državni arhiv u Pazinu**.*

**⭐ 5 October 2026 — four more visitations, one more dean, and the DEANERY'S OWN SEAT.** *Walking folios 100–102 of the same book turned up four more certificates ruled across the page, all in one hand and all naming the place:*

> **«Vidi. PETINAE die 7 Maji 1838»** — *Franc. **Coverlizza**, Decanus*
> **«Vidi … Petinae die 14 Januarii 1839»** — *Coverlizza, Decanus*
> **«Vidi Petinae die 13 Januarii 1840»** — *Coverlizza, Decanus*
> **«Vidi. Petinae die 15 Januarii 1841»** — *Coverlizza, Decanus*

*(doc — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01069113, M01069114, M01069115.)*

**⚠ «Petinae» is PIĆAN — but it is not the only place the dean signs, and [an earlier claim here was withdrawn the same day](/corrections/).** *A sixth certificate, of* **15 March 1849**, *reads* **«Vidi. PIZINAE» — PAZIN** *(M01069123), the letters unmistakable beside the 1838* «Petinae». ***So he signed at Pićan in 1838–1844 and at Pazin in 1849.*** **Both towns are named here and neither is preferred**; *an enquiry should go to whichever archive holds the deanery's papers, and finding that out is part of the item rather than settled by it.*

**Three named deans to ask about now**, *which is far better than a general enquiry:* **Franciscus Franovich** *(1804),* **Petrus Anicich** *(1808)* *and* **Franciscus Coverlizza** *(1838–1841, four inspections in four years — this one was clearly annual).*

*No letter to be sent until David lifts the hold.*

**⭐ 5 October 2026 — AND THE VISITATION WAS NOT THE ONLY THING THE DEANERY DID.** *Folio 98 carries a different certificate entirely:* **«Quae copiae collationatae anni 1835 concordant cum hoc originali libro. Ex officio Decanatus, Petinae die 7 Maij 1836.»** *(M01069111.)* ***The parish copied each year's register and the dean collated the copy against the original.*** **So a certified duplicate set left this parish annually** — *which is [a search of its own](/worklist/) and may matter more than the visitation protocols do.*

**⭐ 5 October 2026, further on — A FOURTH DEAN, and the end of Coverlizza.** *The visitation of* **8 January 1867** *(DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01069145) is signed by a different hand:* **«Jac. Stari—, Decanus»**, *again* «Vidi. Petinae». *He signs again on* **17 January 1868** *(M01069146).* ***Franciscus Coverlizza's run therefore stands at 1838–1865 — twenty-eight years and at least ten recorded inspections*** *— and a new dean takes over by January 1867.*

**⚠ The new dean's surname is NOT published.** *It begins* **Stari-** *and the ending will not resolve —* «-has», «-haz», «-hač» *are all possible, and no second construction of the word has been found.* *[A hand is only legible against itself](/method/); the given name* **Jacobus**, *the office and the date are plain and carry the point.*

**Four named deans to ask about now:** **Franciscus Franovich** *(1804),* **Petrus Anicich** *(1808),* **Franciscus Coverlizza** *(1838–1865)* *and* **Jacobus Stari—** *(1867–1868).*

rows.what: SILESIA — «Amalia Peschle ex Silesia», and the possibility that Carlo's mother's family is German
rows.note:
**David, 1 October 2026: «SILESIA are we going to look for volumes and records for SILESIA? And complete that next line?»** *Yes — and the first job is to narrow «Silesia», because in 1822 it names two different states with two different archive systems.*

**⭐ WHAT WE HAVE. One line, and it is thin.** *At the baptism of* **Clementina Maria Defranceschi, 6 October 1822**, *the godparents are* «Pietro Ant. Defranceschi» *and* **«Amalia PESCHLE ex SILESIA»**, *both entered* **Cives Gollogoricenses**. *(doc — DAPA ZM34K-214, M01069089.)* **That is the whole of it: one godmother, one word, no town.**

**⚠ WHICH SILESIA.** *In a Habsburg register of 1822, «ex Silesia» most likely means* **AUSTRIAN SILESIA** — *the Habsburg duchy around* **Troppau (Opava)** *and* **Teschen (Ciešyn)**, *inside the same monarchy as Istria. **Prussian Silesia** (Breslau, now Wrocław) was a foreign state and would more likely have been said so.* **This is an inference from the politics, not from the entry**, and the entry does not say.

**⭐ AND THE HARDER QUESTION UNDERNEATH IT.** *This archive files the Peschle as a Kvarner family —* «Volosca, on the Kvarner, and Fiume». *But* **Peschle** *is not a Kvarner-looking name, and in Silesia the forms* **Peschel**, **Peschke** *and* **Pöschl** *are ordinary German surnames.* **If the family is German-Silesian in origin, then Volosca and Fiume are where they ARRIVED, not where they came from** — *and [Carlo De Franceschi's mother](/gologorica-line/) is half German. **Nothing establishes that yet.** It is the question the Silesian records would answer.*

**⚠ The name is already unstable in our own books:** *«Peschle» (1826 census), «Pesle» (baptism register, twice, 1821 and 1822). **Any Silesian search must run Peschel, Peschke and Pöschl as well**, or it will return nothing and prove nothing.*

**WHERE THE RECORDS ARE, from [the Record Atlas](../Record Atlas):**

| where | what |
|---|---|
| **Acta Publica** *(`actapublica`)* | **Moravian and Silesian parish registers, free, no account** — the Czech regional archives publish their own; **this is the instrument for Austrian Silesia** |
| **Zemský archiv v Opavě** | *the Opava/Troppau regional archive itself, which holds the Austrian-Silesian registers* — **not yet a provider row in the atlas** |
| Polish state archives *(Prussian Silesia)* | *only if the Austrian side comes up empty; a different country, a different system* |

**ORDER OF WORK, and the first step is free:**

1. **Acta Publica, surname sweep** — *Peschle, Peschel, Peschke, Pöschl across the Silesian parishes, **around 1780–1800** for a woman standing godmother as an adult in 1822.*
2. **Add Zemský archiv v Opavě to the atlas** *if it is not there — [the atlas skill](/method/) asks for the Wikidata id so the postal address comes with it.*
3. **Only then Prussian Silesia**, *and only with a reason.*

**⚠ AND THE HONEST CAVEAT, up front so nobody spends a week on it.** *One godmother in one entry is a **direction**, not a line. She may have been a servant, a visitor, a cousin by marriage, or no relation to Lambertina at all beyond the surname. **What would make this a line is a Silesian Peschle who can be tied to Volosca or Fiume** — and until then this item is a question, not a branch.*

*No letter to be sent until David lifts the hold; Acta Publica needs none.*

---

**⭐ 5 October 2026 — a SECOND raising of the same question, and this time by a household rather than a visitor.**

*At the baptism of* **Conradus Josephus Victorius Peschle**, *28 July 1853 (DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01069128, folio 114), the godparents of a Peschle child are* **«Cost. SCHROTT»** *and* **«Carolina WALSER»**, *entered* **cives**. *The father is* **Dr Albertus Peschle, D.r Medicinæ**, *head of Gologorica house 2; the mother* **Victoria née Calligarich**. *(The household itself was already held from the census — [see the married-in page](/married-in/) — so this is* **verification plus two new names**.)*

**⚠ WHAT IT ADDS, exactly.** *The 1822 evidence was one godmother,* «Amalia Peschle **ex Silesia**». *This is* **two German surnames chosen by a Peschle household for its own child**. ***That is a social circle, not a single visitor***, *and it is the second independent sign that this family moved among German speakers.*

**⚠ WHAT IT DOES NOT ADD.** *Schrott and Walser are German or Austrian;* **neither is Silesian in particular**, *and neither is tied here to any place. A doctor of medicine in Habsburg Istria moved in a German-speaking professional world as a matter of course.* ***This does not shorten the search; it strengthens the reason for it.***

**AND IT ADDS TWO NAMES TO TRY**, *which is worth something concrete: if* **Schrott** *or* **Walser** *turns up beside a Peschle in the Acta Publica sweep of the Silesian parishes, that is a connection rather than a coincidence.*

---

**⭐ 5 October 2026, later the same day — a FOURTH Peschle, and he was summoned from somewhere else.**

*At the baptism of* **Anna Maria Francisca Defranceschi**, *4 November 1860, house 7 (DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01069135, folio 121), the godfather of* [Franciscus Xaverius Defranceschi's](/gologorica-line/) *daughter is* **«ANSELMUS PESCHLE … per procuratorem»** — ***by proxy***, *the formula used when the chosen godparent cannot come and a stand-in holds the child for him. Godmother* «Beatrice Ortis»; *both* **cives**.

**The Peschle this archive has met, in order:**

| who | when | where seen |
|---|---|---|
| **[Lambertina née Peschle](/who/lambertina-defranceschi-peschle/)** | m. 1807, b. 1786 *«Ex Volosca»* | married into the Defranceschi house |
| **Amalia Peschle «ex SILESIA»** | 1822 | godmother at a Defranceschi font |
| **Dr Albertus Peschle**, *D.r Medicinæ* | 1826–1853 | head of Gologorica house 2; *«habitat Pisini»*; his own child's godparents **Schrott** and **Walser** |
| **Anselmus Peschle** | 1860 | godfather **by proxy** — not in the village |

***Four Peschle across fifty years at one small village, one «ex Silesia», one a physician living at Pazin, one summoned in absentia.*** **That is a family with reach, and it is still not a family with an origin.** *A proxy godfather tells you he was away without telling you where — but it is one more reason to believe this name belongs to a dispersed, literate, German-adjacent household rather than a village one.*

**⚠ Still nothing Silesian beyond the single word of 1822.** *The order of work above is unchanged. **Anselmus** joins Peschel, Peschke and Pöschl as a given name to carry into the Acta Publica sweep.*

rows.what: The SECOND series of house numbers in the Gologorica baptism book — what is it?
rows.note:
**Found on 5 October 2026 at the baptism of [Enrichus Jacobus Defranceschi](/who/henricus-jacobus-defranceschi/), and then found to be nothing to do with him.**

*From 1830 the* Domus *cell of this register routinely carries* **two** *numbers: one written, struck through with a diagonal, and a second written beneath. Clean through 1829, scattered in 1830, universal from 1831 on.* **[The full table of pairs is printed on the Gologorica page](/gologorica-line/)** *and is extended every time the walk takes in another folio.*

**⭐ Why it matters to this family.** *The Defranceschi household appears in this one book under* **two** *numbers and always has:* **17** *(1811, 1816, 1822, 1828) and* **104** *(1821, a single clean figure, no strike). If the second series can be identified, that stops being an anomaly and becomes an artefact of how the book was kept — and the [1826* status animarum*](/gologorica-line/), which numbers this household* **7**, *may be a third series.*

**WHAT IT MIGHT BE, none of it established:**

1. *The* **Franciscan cadastre of Istria**, *surveyed around* **1820**, *renumbering the village; this archive already holds a [1820 cadastre note](/gologorica-line/).*
2. *A* **second hamlet's numbering** — *the 1826 census is arranged by* Pagus, *and «Gollogorizia Jacotichi» numbers separately from «Gollogoritia».*
3. *A* **later reviser** *going back over the whole book, which would explain why the doubled cells appear in no chronological order within a page.*

**⚠ No formula fits.** *The second number is usually smaller but not by any constant or ratio: 72→36 is exactly half, 42→18 is not, 93→54 is more than half, 31→12 less.* **Where a pair repeats for the same family it repeats exactly** — *Runco at* **48→23** *in 1830 and again in 1832; the same house at* **6→2** *in 1830 and again in 1833* — *which is the strongest evidence that this is a mapping and not noise.*

**HOW TO SETTLE IT, and it costs nothing:** *keep extending the table as the walk goes on.* **A consistent bijection is a renumbering; a scatter is error.** *Then test the winning series against the house numbers in the 1826, 1862 and 1894* status animarum, *which are on the same reel and have not been read.*

**⚠ Two cautions for whoever takes this up.** *First,* **do not assert the cancelled 1830 Defranceschi number is 17** — *it is not legible; what is legible is that it ends in* **7** *and was replaced by* **104**. *Second,* **read the whole cell before recording a digit**: *the first reading of the Cancinich pair here was* «37→75», *and it is* «37→73» — *the crop had cut the descender off the lower figure. [That one is on the corrections page](/corrections/).*

rows.what: «Antonio Salamon», 1843 — tested against the same scribe's Palman, and it SURVIVES
rows.note:
**Raised and settled on 5 October 2026, within the hour, because the test cost nothing once the frames were in hand.**

*At the baptism of* **Teresia Defranceschi**, *15 November 1843 (DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01069118, folio 104), the godparents of a Defranceschi child are entered* **«Antonio Salamon et Maria soror»**, *conditio* **cives**.

**⚠ WHY IT COULD NOT BE PUBLISHED AS FOUND.** *On 1 October this archive published a* «Franciscus Salman» *of Gologorica beside [Francisca Salomon](/maternal/salomon/), downgraded it on 4 October and* **[withdrew it entirely on 5 October](/corrections/)**: *the family is* **PALMAN**, *and* «Franciscus Palman **filius Stephani**, Sutor» *proved it.* ***It had already been wrong once about an S at the head of this kind of word in this book.***

**⭐ THE TEST, AND IT IS DECISIVE.** *[A hand is only legible against itself](/method/). The scribe of folio 104 is* **Petrus Milcetich**, *and he writes* «Franciscus **Palman** sutor» *on folio 102 (M01069115, 28 April 1841), eleven folios earlier. The two words were cut from the film* **at one magnification** *and set one above the other — [the plate is published](/gologorica-line/):*

| | Palman, 1841 | Salamon, 1843 |
|---|---|---|
| **initial** | *tall closed majuscule bowl* | *small low pointed stroke, no bowl* |
| **body** | *a · l · m · a · n* | *a · l · **a** · m · **o** · n* |
| **letters** | six | seven |

***The medial «a» between the l and the m is the clincher.*** **The 1843 word is not Palman.**

**WHAT IS NOW ESTABLISHED:** *a man surnamed* **Salamon**, *entered* **civis**, *with* «Maria soror» *beside him, standing godfather to a Defranceschi child at Gologorica in 1843. A household, not a stray name.*

**⚠ WHAT IS NOT:** *any connection to Francisca Salomon's people.* **That needs this Antonio Salamon tied to Gračišće**, *and nothing here does it.* *[Worklist 174](/worklist/) carries what would.*

rows.what: Two roster rows for one Teresia — RESOLVED with `sameAs`, the archive's own precedent
rows.note:
**Raised and closed on 5 October 2026 — and it should never have been raised as David's decision.**

*This archive held* **two** *rows for the daughter of* **Antonius Defranceschi and Francisca**, *born* **14 November 1843** *at Gologorica house 5:* `teresia-defranceschi-1843` *and* `theresia-defranceschi-1843`, *one spelt with an h.* **The register names her TERESIA, without it.**

**It was put to David on the ground that retiring either row would break a published address.** *That ground was right; the conclusion was not.* ***Twenty-nine other rows in this roster already carry a*** `sameAs` ***field*** *saying «this row and that row are one person» — it retires nothing, moves no id, keeps both addresses alive and stops the count lying.*

**Applied:** `theresia-defranceschi-1843` *is marked* `sameAs: teresia-defranceschi-1843`. **[Written up on the corrections page](/corrections/)**, *because the error worth recording is not the duplicate — it is that a session escalated a question the archive had already answered twenty-nine times.* ***Before escalating, grep for how the same shape was settled before.***

**Still worth doing, and now the only part left:** *a sweep for other pairs sharing a birth year, a parent pair and a name differing by one letter. The* `sameAs` *mechanism makes it safe and cheap.*

rows.what: Antonio Salamon of Gologorica, 1843 — turn the surviving lead into a line, or kill it
rows.note:
**[Worklist 172](/worklist/) established that the 1843 godfather's surname is SALAMON and not Palman**, *by setting the word beside the same scribe's Palman at one magnification.* **That is a lead on [the Salomon maternal line](/maternal/salomon/) and it is not yet a line.** *What is held is one entry:* «**Antonio Salamon et Maria soror**», *cives, standing for* [Teresia Defranceschi](/person/teresia-defranceschi-1843/) *on* **15 November 1843** *at Gologorica house 5.*

**THE ORDER OF WORK, cheapest first, and all of it is in frames the family already holds:**

1. **Sweep the rest of this baptism book for Salamon.** *Folios 105 to the end (M01069119–M01069181, about 63 frames) are unread, and folios 1–104 were read for* **Defranceschi** *— not for Salamon.* ***A second pass of the read folios specifically for this surname costs nothing but attention***, *and a man with a sister at Gologorica in 1843 should have children, a marriage or a burial in the same parish.*
2. **The 1826 *status animarum*** *(M01069315–M01069435) was walked end to end and no Salamon was recorded — but it was being read for* **Defranceschi** *wives, and a godfather's household is exactly the kind of thing such a reading passes over.* **Worth one targeted re-look at the household index.**
3. **The Gologorica death register 1784–1880** *(M01069224–M01069314, 91 frames,* ***2% read***) *— if he died in the parish it names his age and often his birthplace, which is what would tie him to Gračišće or rule it out.*
4. **Only then Gračišće.** *Francisca Salomon's own parish is on* **ZM34K-216**, *the one reel of this set the family does not hold, and [getting it is already the first errand](/errands/).*

**⚠ AND THE DISCIPLINE THAT GOT THIS FAR, written down so it is not lost:** *the Salman lead was published, downgraded and withdrawn across six days because it was written up before it was tested.* **This one was tested before it was written up.** *Every further step here states which it is.*

rows.what: Anastasia · Maria Adelgidis · Adelaidis — three names, one birth year, possibly one daughter
rows.note:
**Raised 5 October 2026 by the entry that [placed Adelaidis](/who/adelaidis-defranceschi/).**

*Three sources describe a daughter of* **Josephus Defranceschi and Lambertina née Peschle** *born in* **1824**, *and they do not use the same name:*

| source | name | date |
|---|---|---|
| the family tree / pedigree | **Anastasia** | **8 December 1824** |
| the 1826 *status animarum*, house 7 | **Maria Adelgidis** | *listed sixth of ten children* |
| this roster, imported from the live tree 20 Sept 2026 | **Adelaidis** | **1824**, unplaced until today |

**The 1847 baptism register names* «Maximilianus Defranceschi **et soror Adelaidis**» *— so Adelaidis is certainly their daughter.* **What is not certain is whether she and Anastasia are the same child or two.**

**WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, cheapest first:**

1. **The baptism itself.** *December 1824 falls around folio* **78–80** *of this book (roughly M01069091–M01069093), which have been read for the surname but not re-read for a given name.* ***One targeted look at the December 1824 entries answers it outright*** *— the register will have written whichever name she was christened with, and if there are two girls there are two entries.*
2. *The* **1826 census, house 7** *(M01069332) is already transcribed; re-read it for whether an Anastasia appears anywhere in the household.*
3. *The* **death register** *(M01069224–M01069314), for either name.*

**⚠ Nothing is merged until step 1 is done.** *[A person id is minted once and frozen](/method/); retiring a row on a suspicion breaks a published address for a saving of one line in a count.* **And a family that demonstrably reused the name Clementina for two daughters is a family that could have had both an Anastasia and an Adelgidis.**

rows.what: RE-READ THE MARGINS — somebody closed lives in this baptism book decades later, and this archive has been reading past them
rows.note:
**Noticed on 5 October 2026 at folio 109, after four of them turned up in a handful of frames.**

*The Gologorica baptism register carries* **death dates written into baptism entries by a later hand**, *sometimes seventy years after the event:*

| person | baptised | margin |
|---|---|---|
| **[Rosa Defranceschi](/person/joanna-defranceschi-1848/)** | 8 June 1848 | **† 10 Dec 1899** |
| **[Leonardus Defranceschi](/who/leonardus-defranceschi/)** | 23 Jan 1847 | **† 20 Dec 1917** |
| *Antonius Sestan, son of [Sancta Alexandra](/who/sancta-alexandra-defranceschi-sestan/)* | 27 Mar 1848 | **† 27 Aug 1923** |
| *Antonius Gasparich* | 4 June 1830 | **† 4 Mar 1898** |

**⚠ WHY THIS IS A WORKLIST ITEM AND NOT JUST AN OBSERVATION.** *This archive has walked roughly a hundred folios of this book reading the* **entry**. *The margins were seen and passed over as annotation.* ***They are a death register hiding inside a baptism register***, *and they close dates this archive has been recording as unknown — Rosa's fifty-one years were a blank until this afternoon.*

**WHAT TO DO, and it is cheap because the frames are already in hand:**

1. **Re-read every Defranceschi entry already found**, *for its margin alone. About thirty entries across folios 1–109.*
2. *Carry the margins forward as part of the walk from folio 110 on —* **done from this row onward**.
3. *Where a margin gives a death, say so on the person's page and mark it* **doc**, *naming frame and folio.*

**⚠ And a caution.** *A marginal* «†» *with a bare day and two-digit year —* «† 10/12 99» — *is ambiguous about century on its face.* **It is not ambiguous in practice here**, *because the subject's own baptism fixes the only century that can follow it; but the reading should always be stated with the baptism beside it, as [Rosa's is](/person/joanna-defranceschi-1848/).*

---

**✔ STEP 1 DONE, 5 October 2026 — and the answer is a caution rather than a harvest.**

*Every Defranceschi baptism this archive has found in the first hundred folios was re-cropped and read for its margin alone:*

| entry | frame | margin |
|---|---|---|
| Maria Aloysia, 1811 | M01069070 | *— none* |
| Franciscus Xaverius, 1816 | M01069078 | **† 4 January 1893** *(already held)* |
| Clementina, 1821 | M01069086 | *— none* |
| Clementina Maria, 1822 | M01069089 | *— none* |
| Maximilianus Antonius, 1828 | M01069098 | **† 6 August 1910** *(already held)* |
| Enrichus Jacobus, 1830 | M01069102 | *— none* |

**No new deaths. Both margins that exist were already read.**

**⚠ AND THE REAL RESULT IS THE CALIBRATION.** *On folio 73 only* **one of three** *entries carries a dagger; on folio 89,* **one of five**. ***The later keeper's work is partial, so a blank margin is not evidence that anybody lived.*** *That matters immediately: the 1821 Clementina has no dagger, and [this archive's inference that she died young](/gologorica-line/) is neither supported nor refuted by it.* **Nobody should read a silent margin as a life.**

**Step 2 — carrying margins forward from folio 110 — remains, and is now part of every row of the walk.**

rows.what: Two Antonius Defranceschi of 1855, five years apart on the death — one man or two?
rows.note:
**Raised 5 October 2026 the moment the register supplied a date that collided.**

| row | born | died | source | line |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`antonius-defranceschi-1853`](/person/antonius-defranceschi-1853/) | **3 February 1855** *(register)* | **17 February 1913** *(register margin)* | **doc** — DAPA ZM34K-214, M01069130 | carnia, Gologorica, son of Antonius & Francisca |
| [`antonius-defranceschi-1855`](/person/antonius-defranceschi-1855/) | 1855 | **1918** | MyHeritage tree | *unknown*, no place |

**Same name, same birth year, and the death years are five apart.**

**⚠ WHY THIS IS NOT MERGED.** *[A death year is usually the better-evidenced of the two](/corrections/), so a five-year gap usually means* ***one side is describing a different man of the same name in the same parish*** *— which is exactly what this archive concluded twice before, for [Clementina](/person/clementina-maria-defranceschi-1822/) and [Josephus Lambertus](/who/josephus-lambertus-defranceschi/), and has not yet resolved in either case.* **Three unresolved death-year collisions in one family is itself a finding**, *and it points at one book.*

**WHAT SETTLES IT, and it is the same answer all three times:** *the* **Gologorica death register 1784–1880** *(M01069224–M01069314,* **91 frames**, *about 2% read).* ***This is now the strongest reason to open that book***, *and it would close Clementina, Josephus Lambertus and this Antonius in one walk.*

**⚠ Do not assume the margin wins.** *The 1913 date is a later hand writing in a baptism register sixty years on; the 1918 is a family tree. Both are second-hand to the death itself. The burial entry is first-hand and neither of these is.*

rows.what: THE DUPLICATE REGISTERS — a certified second copy left this parish every year. Where did it go?
rows.note:
**Found 5 October 2026 in the strip at the foot of folio 98, which this archive had been [cropping off every page all day](/corrections/).**

> **«Quae copiae collationatae anni 1835 concordant cum hoc originali libro. Ex officio Decanatus, Petinae die 7 Maij 1836.»**

*(doc — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01069111.)* ***The parish copied each year's register; the dean collated the copy against the original and certified that the two agreed.*** **So a second, certified set of these books went out of Gologorica annually, and the film holds the one that stayed.**

**⭐ WHY THIS MAY MATTER MORE THAN ANYTHING ELSE ON THIS LIST.**

1. **[The reel the family does not hold.](/errands/)** *Gračišće — where [Francisca](/person/francisca-defranceschi-1819/), [Joanna](/who/joanna-defranceschi-sestan/) and probably [Lucia](/who/lucia-defranceschi/) were born — is on* **ZM34K-216**. *If Gračišće sent annual copies to the same deanery,* ***there is a second route to the same entries***.
2. **[The three death-year collisions.](/gologorica-line/)** *A duplicate death register is a second chance at the same burials.*
3. **An independent third reading** *wherever [this register and the 1826 census disagree](/gologorica-line/) — and they disagree on five of Joanna's eight children.*

**⚠ WHAT IS NOT KNOWN, AND IT IS NEARLY EVERYTHING.** *Whether the duplicates* **survive**; *where they went after the deanery; whether the practice ran for more than the one year this certificate covers; whether Gračišće did the same.* ***This archive has not looked and is not claiming they exist.*** **What it now knows is that they were MADE** — *which is the difference between a search with a target and a search without one.*

**WHERE TO LOOK, in order:**

1. *The* **Državni arhiv u Pazinu** *finding aids for* **deanery** *(dekanat) and* **diocesan** *fonds, as distinct from parish fonds — the atlas already lists DAPA and [it is already on the errands](/errands/) for other reasons.*
2. *The* **diocesan archive at Poreč**, *which took the Pićan material after 1788 and is [also already on the errands list](/errands/).*
3. *Ask both in the same letter as the reel request*, ***naming this certificate and its date***, *because an archivist can answer «do you hold the deanery duplicates» far faster than they can answer «what do you have».*

*No letter to be sent until David lifts the hold — but this changes what the letters should ask for.*

rows.what: ⭐ LEONARDO DE FRANCESCHI, LUINCIS, 23 JUNE 1626 — a 1920 state act names him. Find the act, then find the book
rows.note:
**Found 5 October 2026 on folio 142 of the Gologorica baptism register — a typewritten slip pasted across two entries of July 1871, the only typewriting in a book of handwriting.**

> **«Giusta lettera del Commissariato Gen. Civ. per la Venezia Giulia dd 10/12 1920 N. 1x-4411/563 la grafia originale del cognome di questo battezzato è “de Franceschi”, ciò che risulta dalla fede di nascita del suo proavo LEONARDO DE FRANCESCHI nato a LUINCIO dd. 23/6 1626. D’Ordine del Commissariato Gen. Civ. — Avv. Melone»**

*(doc — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01069151, folio 142. [The story is told on the Carnia page](/carnia/) and [on the Gologorica page](/gologorica-line/).)*

**⭐ WHY THIS IS THE BIGGEST LEAD ON THIS LIST.** *[The Carnia chain](/carnia/) begins with a* **Leonardo de Franceschi** *dead before 1785, known only from his son’s styling; its deepest document is a parish certificate of 1808 reaching a* **Giovanni Battista** *dead by 1789 — and that certificate was written* «a parte **Luvincis**» *by the priest of the* **Pieve Matrice di Gorto**. ***An Italian state official in 1920 cites the same parish’s Book of Baptisms for 1626 and names a man in it.*** **Which also means the 1626 volume existed in 1920.**

**TARGET 1 — THE ACT, and it is the easier of the two.** *A numbered, dated act of a named office:* **Commissariato Generale Civile per la Venezia Giulia, 10 December 1920, protocol N. 1x-4411/563**.

* *The Commissariato’s records are* **state records of the Kingdom of Italy**, *and the obvious holder is the* **Archivio di Stato di Trieste**, *which took the civil administration’s papers.*
* *An enquiry citing* **the exact protocol number and date** *is the kind an archivist can answer in one search — far better than a general question about a surname.*
* ***The file should contain or cite the* fede di nascita *itself***, *which is what this archive actually wants.*

**TARGET 2 — THE BOOK.** *The baptisms of the* **Pieve di Gorto at Luincis (Ovaro, Udine) for 1626**.

* *[The Record Atlas](../Record Atlas) and the* **Antenati** *portal are the first look; Udine’s diocesan and state archives the second.*
* *This archive [already quotes the Gorto Book of Baptisms](/carnia/) at second hand, through the 1808 certificate.* ***It has never read the book.***

**⚠ AND THE DISCIPLINE, because this is exactly the kind of find that gets over-read.**

1. *It is a* **1920 ruling, not a 1626 record**. *An official says the certificate existed and says what it said.*
2. **«Proavo» is loose** — *great-grandfather by the dictionary, forefather in use; 1626 to 1871 is seven or eight generations.*
3. **The office had a motive.** *A body regularising surnames after annexation wants a spelling settled, and a settled spelling is not a proved descent.* ***Nothing shows the official traced the line; it shows he accepted it.***
4. ***No generation has been added to the Carnia chain on the strength of it***, *and none will be until the book is read.*

**⚠ And the slip hides the entry it annotates**, *so this archive cannot read the 1871 baptism underneath. [The duplicate registers of worklist 178](/worklist/) would have it uncovered — which is the first time those two items have pointed at the same page.*

*No letter to be sent until David lifts the hold — but of everything on this list, this is the one where a single enquiry with a protocol number could answer a question the archive has carried since it began.*

close: **Four things are waiting on people rather than on searching**: Ovaro's undigitised registers, the Y-DNA test, the three archive request forms that need David's own data, and a 404 page that belongs to another session. Everything else here is either finished or is a book that can be opened tonight.
